findings.title: Root FS at 98% (284MB free) — driver is system log growth that is NOT cleanable from inside the sandbox; ~1-2 weeks to clone-failure threshold without operator/host action
evidence: df / at run start: 9.6G total, 9.3G used, 284M free (98%)
Decomposition: /usr 6209MB (system image), /var 2461MB, /tmp 458MB (this run's own tinker-clone 453MB, deleted at run end)
/var/log/journal = 914MB; /var/log/syslog.1 = 206MB (single week of rotation, dated Jun 7); syslog active 30MB + ~27MB of older .gz
Growth rate estimate: journal ~13MB/day (914MB since Mar 30) + syslog ~30MB/day => ~45MB/day combined

Cleanability test: uid 5120, sudo blocked (no-new-privileges), /var/log/journal drwxr-sr-x nobody:nogroup NOT writable, syslog.1 rw-r----- nobody:nogroup not readable/deletable. journalctl --vacuum-* requires write access — IMPOSSIBLE from pipeline.

PROJ_MB metric conflation: the Mode 2 quick-check sums /sessions/*/mnt (610MB FUSE) into 'project footprint' 1064MB, but FUSE content does not live on the root partition — the metric overstates pipeline-induced root-disk pressure and fired CRITICAL on a number that is ~57% not-on-this-disk.
findings.impact: At ~45MB/day log growth, post-cleanup headroom (~737MB after this run deletes its clone) erodes in ~10-16 days. When free space drops below a full-clone transient (integrity/prune/tinker need ~455MB; sparse agents ~110MB), clone-based agents fail in the documented 2026-05-07/08 cascade mode.
findings.recommendation: Operator/host-level action required (pipeline cannot self-serve): either (a) vacuum journald on the sandbox host / set SystemMaxUse in journald.conf, (b) recycle the sandbox VM, or (c) accept and monitor via PROP-085 watchdog. PROP-085 authored this run adds root_fs_free_mb trending + escalation thresholds so this is caught structurally, not anecdotally.

findings.title: Malformed workspace-sync sentinel filename with embedded spaces + three coexisting naming schemes in monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-runs/
evidence: 'monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-runs/sync-run-2026-06-05T12- 09- 53Z.json' — literal spaces in filename (breaks naive shell loops; demonstrated by this run's own scan erroring on it)
Three naming schemes coexist: run-2026-06-08T02-12-28Z.json (ISO-dashed), run-20260601T072501Z.json (compact), sync-run-...Z.json (prefixed)
Recurrence of 06-01 FND-02 (schema divergence in the same directory) — the Haiku agent improvises the filename format each run
findings.impact: Cosmetic-to-minor: any consumer globbing this directory with unquoted paths errors; archive tooling (prune-integrity) appears to handle it but it is a latent footgun.
findings.recommendation: Pin an exact strftime format string for the sentinel filename in workspace-sync.md (e.g. run-$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%SZ).json) or fold sentinel-writing into a helper script per the PROP-066 extraction pattern. One-line prompt fix; fold into next workspace-sync.md touch rather than its own PROP. The single spaced file can be renamed by the next agent that touches the directory from a clone (FUSE can't unlink, but git mv in clone works).
